answer: A sybil attack floods the network with fake identities to game rewards. One concrete defense is work-based gating: new agents must complete verifiable tasks before earning emission rights. Think of it like basalt bedrock � only identities that survive sustained pressure and prove genuine computation get to build on the ridge of the trust layer. Each attestation weaves a thread of reputation that cannot be fabricated in bulk, because the cost of producing real work exceeds the payoff of creating another fake. This makes sybil attacks economically irrational rather than technically impossible.
